blocks.prompt: 9 Given the function \(f(x) = \ln x\). Find the equation of the transformed function after applying in order, the vertical stretch by factor 4, shift 6 units to right, horizontal compress by factor 3, and shift 1 unit upward. Draw the graphs of both the original and transformed functions on the same coordinate plane.
blocks.explanation:
Four transformations in order, then two graphs.
Plan: stretch by 4 (multiply by 4), right 6 (\(x \to x - 6\)), compress by 3 (\(x \to 3x\)), up 1 (add 1); then plot both, using the moved asymptote.
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = \ln x\), \(x > 0\).
To find: the transformed function \(g\), and draw \(f\) and \(g\) together.
Method: \(y = 4f(x)\); \(y = g(x - 6)\); \(y = g(3x)\); then add 1, each on the newest function.

Step 1: vertical stretch by 4
\[g_{1}(x) = 4\ln x\]
Why: \(a = 4\) multiplies all outputs.

Step 2: shift 6 units right
\[g_{2}(x) = 4\ln(x - 6)\]
Why: every \(x\) of \(g_{1}\) becomes \(x - 6\).

Step 3: horizontal compression by 3
\[g_{3}(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6)\]
Why: every \(x\) of \(g_{2}\) becomes \(3x\): \(x - 6 \to 3x - 6\).

Step 4: shift 1 unit up
\[g(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6) + 1\]
Why: up 1 adds 1 to every output.

Features for the graph of g
\[3x - 6 > 0 \Rightarrow x > 2\]
\[g\left(\tfrac{7}{3}\right) = 4\ln 1 + 1 = 1\]
\[g(3) = 4\ln 3 + 1 \approx 5.39\]
\[g(4) = 4\ln 6 + 1 \approx 8.17\]
\[x\text{-intercept}: x = 2 + \tfrac{1}{3}e^{-1/4} \approx 2.26\]
Why: the asymptote \(x = 0\) of \(\ln x\) moves to \(x = 6\) and then to \(x = \frac{6}{3} = 2\); the \(x\)-intercept solves \(\ln(3x - 6) = -\frac{1}{4}\).

Draw both graphs
\(f(x) = \ln x\): asymptote \(x = 0\), through \((1, 0)\) and \((e, 1)\). \(g\): asymptote \(x = 2\), through \(\left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\), \((3, 5.39)\), \((4, 8.17)\); it rises 4 times as fast as \(\ln x\).
Why: the plotted points and asymptotes fix each curve.

Check:
Follow \((1, 0)\) of \(\ln x\): stretch \(\to (1, 0)\); right 6 \(\to (7, 0)\); compress \(\to \left(\frac{7}{3}, 0\right)\); up 1 \(\to \left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\), and indeed \(g\left(\frac{7}{3}\right) = 1\).
blocks.final_answer: \(g(x) = 4\ln(3x - 6) + 1\), \(x > 2\); its graph has the asymptote \(x = 2\) and passes through \(\left(\frac{7}{3}, 1\right)\), drawn with \(f(x) = \ln x\) in the figure.

answer_figure.alt: The curve f(x) = ln x through (1, 0) with the y-axis as asymptote, and the curve g(x) = 4 ln(3x - 6) + 1 rising steeply from the dashed asymptote x = 2 through (7/3, 1), (3, 5.39) and (4, 8.17).
answer_figure.caption: f(x) = ln x and g(x) = 4 ln(3x − 6) + 1
